changes: Outer launch/configuration/JSON exceptions produce FAILED receipts and exact private SSH stdout/stderr; private exception detail kept out of public receipt.
Nested host/VM readers retain per-command errors and continue where possible; each call has timeout, sum of remote command budgets39s within local SSH55s (nested dmesg15s).
Public stderr is size/hash only. Host process capture remains pid/ppid/rss/comm; no args/env, mutation or workload command. Guest Python adds -B; sudo -n prevents interactive prompt.

Boot IDs captured before/after kernel read; CAPTURED requires successful reads and matching valid IDs. OOM selection retains exact decoded line text/line number, with complete SSH payload privately hashed.
PARTIAL_CAPTURE and FAILED do not imply no OOM; selected lines are whole boot-buffer observations, not cell-specific filtering or worker attribution. Exclusive output refuses overwrite.
limitations: No SSH, Colima, Docker, host sysctl, ps or dmesg execution in this review; all invocation paths mocked.
Caller must establish cell termination. Local SSH timeout does not establish remote-reader termination; per-command budgets are not a hard wall-clock guarantee for remote process startup.
Exact outer SSH bytes retained; nested dmesg text is decoded by Python. The public dmesg hash explicitly describes decoded UTF-8 re-encoding, not an independent raw kernel-byte hash.
Public receipt requires writable output storage. If private storage fails, explicit retention_errors and FAILED are recorded; no impossible guarantee of retained bytes during disk/permission failure.
Snapshot records only command-time pressure/boot/kernel evidence; it neither establishes per-cell physical I/O nor diagnoses cause or worker identity.
changed_scope: Only new collect_host_closure.py; local mock script/logs/receipt outside repository. Prior runner/config/prose and captured evidence were not edited.
